reports.name: Fistulina hepatica
reports.shape: A selected broad red tongue-like bracket is laterally attached to an explicitly contextual woody support. Its rounded outline, closed margin and separate lower tubules replace the old undifferentiated disc and pebble-like support.
reports.surface: Darker red numerical pigment, muted wet sheen, fine upper papillae and pale open-ended tubule relief. No reference-photo pixels or calibrated reflectance.
reports.remaining: The bracket outline and attachment still look authored, tubule positions are idealized and bark support is contextual artwork. Fine tissue structure, guttation, age variation, real optical response, hyphal physiology and dimensions remain unmeasured or absent.

reports.name: Laetiporus sulphureus
reports.shape: Ten selected overlapping lateral shelves have continuous rounded margins and attached pore-bearing lower skins, with a connected woody context rather than a generic mushroom stem.
reports.surface: Orange upper interiors transition to broader sulphur-yellow margins; lower pore cues and original numerical fine relief distinguish the upper and fertile surfaces.
reports.remaining: Shelf spacing and pore placement remain too regular, some shelves intersect, and the model is less densely overlapping than the reference. Host/region-dependent species limits, fine pore anatomy, age and tissue optics remain unresolved or unmeasured.

reports.name: Cerioporus squamosus
reports.shape: Two selected depressed caps have shorter thick eccentric stems, dark basal cues, rolled thinner margins and a coarse angular lower pore field. Polyporus squamosus is a synonym, not an additional species.
reports.surface: Buff caps bear varied raised brown radial/concentric scale patches. Numeric pore relief, muted stem pigment and dark bases remain on the same geometry across display actions.
reports.remaining: Scale placement still has visible concentric regularity, depressions and rolled margins are simplified, and the cap/stipe proportions are unmeasured. Decurrent pore architecture, fine hyphae, tissue optics and host attachment remain partial.

reports.name: Schizophyllum commune
reports.shape: Selected laterally attached shell-like bodies expose paired radial split pseudolamellar folds beneath thin hairy caps. The woody orientation is a selected contextual study, not the photographed individual.
reports.surface: Pale densely modeled hairs, lighter margins and pinkish-grey paired lower folds replace blank dark undersides. Original relief and pigment are retained across actions.
reports.remaining: The seven cap arrangement is more regular and less crowded than the photograph. Fine split-fold edges, branching/anastomosis, hyphal hairs and tissue optics are incomplete. No measured moisture response or independent lineage identification.

reports.name: Sparassis crispa
reports.shape: A mounded assembly of 180 thin curled flabellae connects to a branched base; the old floating disc and the rejected initial forest of separate stalks are replaced.
reports.surface: Warm cream/buff original numerical pigment and crinkled thin surfaces replace generic spherical florets. Fold relief is geometric rather than a photographic texture.
reports.remaining: Folds remain too regular, pointed and ribbon-like in places; the underside branch fan is simplified. Natural frond edge lobing, tissue translucency, developmental branching, dimensions and species-complex variation remain incomplete.

reports.name: Hericium erinaceus
reports.shape: A selected European cream-white sessile lobed mass has dense shorter downward teeth over smaller connected lobes. It is distinct from the older broad-name North Carolina draft reference.
reports.surface: Original cream pigment and dense pendent tooth geometry; no generated photograph or source-pixel material. Lobes and tooth density remain a partial authored phenotype study.
reports.remaining: Lobes remain too rounded and some upper surfaces too smooth; tooth insertion, maturation and cream/brown age variation are incomplete. The source-labelled European image is not a molecular voucher, and broad-name occurrence assignments still need specialist reconciliation.

reports.name: Hydnum repandum
reports.shape: Two selected irregular rolled buff caps on shorter robust pale stipes bear dense downward teeth and partial tooth cues descending around the upper stipes. No woody bracket support is substituted for this terrestrial ectomycorrhizal fungus.
reports.surface: Muted apricot/buff numerical cap pigment, matte pale supports and geometric lower teeth distinguish it from translucent Pseudohydnum.
reports.remaining: Cap ripples and tooth placement are still regular, stipe/edge structure is simplified and proportions unmeasured. Original photo geography and narrow-species identification remain unresolved; microscopic traits, mycorrhizae and tissue optics are not simulated.

reports.name: Pseudohydnum gelatinosum
reports.shape: A selected single laterally attached gelatinous fruit body has a broad curved support, brownish upper tongue and much smaller pale lower teeth, distinct from opaque terrestrial Hydnum.
reports.surface: Lower-opacity warm grey/brown numerical surfaces and a subdued wet sheen replace the first opaque oyster-like shelves. Subsurface scattering and measured translucency are not solved.
reports.remaining: The jelly's internal scattering, water content, fine surface microtexture and optical thickness remain uncalibrated. Cap/support proportions and pore-tooth microanatomy are simplified; regional species-complex assignments remain source-labelled.

limits: Partly stylized, unmeasured original educational reconstructions. Fine anatomy, age variation, tissue optics, dimensions and physiology remain incomplete. Enlarged spore dots are a teaching overlay with authored timing, not measured release, Buller-drop mechanics or an airflow solver. No independent specialist validation, scientific certification or accuracy percentage.
